[A kid telling a spooky-funny story at a sleepover, fast and gleeful, every sentence a bit more excited, one breath, punching the key word; full voice, never whispering]

My village is covered in nine thousand carpets. The road? Carpet. The stairs? Carpet. The doghouse? Also carpet. We shear three hundred sheep every morning to keep up. Even our bell is wrapped in white wool. The dog on the hill hasn't moved in nine-hundred days. Not for rain. Not for thunder. Not for creepers. Not even zombies. I bring him a bone every morning. He never looks.
